title: Runtime Integration Check-in — Sprint 30 (kernel, KV cache, batching)
content:
Attendees: Aisha (owner), Matt, Sofia, Ben, Ava, Ravi; quick async inputs from Neil and Hannah.

Purpose: mid-sprint integration check focused on three cross-cutting risks that bubbled up in last week’s CI runs and customer replay: kernel stability (new fused-attention), KV cache eviction behaviour on multi-tenant hosts, and batching heuristics causing tail latency spikes for short requests.

Agenda:
- Brief status updates (5m)
- Kernel regression investigation & patch plan (20m)
- KV cache eviction policy experiments & metrics (20m)
- Batching heuristics: backpressure + adaptive windows (15m)
- Action items & owners (5m)

Notes (high level):
1) Kernel regression (fused-attention v2)
- Symptom: after landing fused-attention v2 (PR 4692) we saw intermittent 95th/99th latency regressions on long-context GPT-style models under moderate concurrency. Not reproducible locally with unit/integration harness but visible on heavy CI runs and a customer replay (cust-replay-rt-07-21).
- Root-cause hypothesis: kernel scheduling sometimes leaves small micro-pauses when preempting kernels for other streams; combined with our KV cache prefetch path this yields cascading stalls.
- Data: two reproducible traces from CI where a single long request (len 4k tokens) interleaved with many short ones shows 100–300ms extra latency on token emission at tail. Trace ids: trace-ci-7601, trace-cust-07-21-A.
- Interim mitigation: roll-out hold on fused-attention v2 to canary nodes; rollback plan staged across 3 waves if we see >10% 95th-latency regression on canaries.
- Fix plan: Ben to add lightweight scheduling fairness counters in runtime to capture kernel switch frequency and preempt durations; Aisha + Ben to instrument in 4692 branch. If metrics show high preempt churn, we either (a) add a micro-scheduling window to coalesce fused kernels or (b) add a backoff in KV prefetch to avoid starting large prefetches during peak switching.
- Timeline: instrumenting + short-run CI by Thu 2026-07-30; decision point Fri 2026-07-31 to either proceed with patch or rollback.

2) KV cache eviction behaviour on multi-tenant hosts
- Symptom: host-level memory pressure sometimes triggers aggressive eviction of prefetched KV shards causing cache-miss storms for tenant A leading to throughput drop. Reported by SRE during a nightly soak.
- Findings: eviction currently uses a global LRU across tenants with simple memory threshold heuristics. Under uneven token shapes (few large contexts + many small sessions) LRU favors large hot entries but loses many small but frequently accessed prefixes.
- Experiment results: Sofia ran a 48h soak with modified scoring that adds access-frequency weighting and penalizes very-large entries; initial results: 6% reduction in token load-miss rate for tenant mixes in the staging scenario, 4% improvement in average throughput under contention. However a regression was observed for a synthetic workload that relies on very long contiguous contexts (weaker hit rate for those contexts).
- Proposal: implement a two-tier eviction policy: small-prefix cache (freq-biased) + large-prefix stable cache (size-aware). Also expose tenant-level cache quotas to Dedicated customers (opt-in GA flag).
- Action: Sofia to open RW-2254 with experiment artifacts and config knobs; Ravi to prototype quota enforcement in the private cache manager. MVP for staging by 2026-08-12.

3) Batching heuristics & short-request tail spikes
- Symptom: at QPS ~2k with mixed payloads we see tail latency spikes (~400–600ms) for short requests (<=12 tokens). Investigation points to batching windows that prioritize filling batch size over latency under transient bursts.
- Recent change: adaptive-window code increases window to 8ms to improve throughput; but when many short requests arrive in microbursts the batching timer sometimes waits, creating tail spikes.
- Decisions discussed:
  - Add a short-request fast-path: if request predicted <=12 tokens and queueing time exceeds 1.2ms, force immediate flush (no batching).
  - Use client-side hints: add optional header X-Estimate-Tokens to steer server batching decisions for latency-sensitive endpoints. SDKs to support this as opt-in.
  - Monitor for fairness: ensure large-gen workloads aren't starved by aggressive short-path flushing.
- Action: Ava to prototype fast-path flush for short requests + metrics (p99/p50) in canary; SDK team (DevX) to add header support. Measure false-positive/negative rate of token estimation over next two weeks.

4) Operational items & observability improvements
- Add new dashboards: kernel-switch-frequency, kv-eviction-by-tenant, batching-queue-depth-by-model. Matt to own dashboard queries and alert thresholds. Expected deliverable: dashboards + runbook entry by 2026-08-05.
- Add regression test in CI: synthetic mixed workload harness that reproduces customer replay patterns (long-with-short interleaving). Neil to add harness; target green by 2026-08-01.

5) Open questions / risks
- Does adding tenant quotas for KV cache materially change tail latencies for large-context customers? Need e2e canary validation.
- How reliable will client side X-Estimate-Tokens be in practice? SDK adoption risk.
- Are there scheduler-level improvements that require GPU-driver or runtime-kernel collaboration (beyond our user-space changes)? May need infra sync with hardware team.

Action items (owner — due):
- Ben: Add scheduling fairness counters in fused-attn branch + submit instrumentation PR (due 2026-07-30).
- Aisha & Ben: Evaluate instrumentation on canaries and decide rollback vs patch (decision 2026-07-31).
- Sofia: Finalize RW-2254 experiment notes & create config knobs PR for two-tier eviction (2026-08-05).
- Ravi: Prototype tenant quota enforcement in cache manager (2026-08-12).
- Ava: Implement short-request fast-path flush and add p99/p50 telemetry (canary 2026-08-03).
- Matt: Dashboards + runbook entry for new metrics (2026-08-05).
- Neil: Add mixed-workload regression harness to CI, wire up nightly job (2026-08-01).

Notes to self / discussion fragments (informal):
- "if we can't get scheduling stable, roll back fused-attn v2 this Friday. customer replay is sensitive; don't over-optimize until we have stable prefetch interactions."
- "short path heuristics should be framable as opt-in experiment; don't change defaults mid-sprint without clear canary success."
- "SRE: consider temporary heavier eviction thresholds during high-noise maintain windows."

Meeting capture / quick timeline:
- 07/28 09:30: Kickoff + triage
- 07/28 10:00: Deep-dive w/ Ben on kernel traces
- 07/28 11:15: KV eviction experiment review (Sofia)
- 07/28 14:00: Batching heuristics workshop (Ava)

Small appendix (metrics snapshot from staging, taken 2026-07-27):
- Mixed-workload QPS: 2.1k
- Average token latency baseline: 12.4ms
- 95th before fused-attn v2: 62ms; after: 81ms (on canary cluster during CI runs)
- KV cache hit rate tenant-mix A: 87% -> 81% under eviction storm
- Short-request p99: 210ms -> spikes to 580ms under batching microbursts

References / links: see linked_artifacts above.

If anything missing ping me in slack thread linked in linked_artifacts.
